title: Space clause of (40a) is unattainable; (40a) reduces to its update-time clause
statement: Myhill-Nerode count: for L = MCSP^A[s] on N = 2^m bits and any prefix length k, distinct nonempty residual classes {v : uv in L} <= #yes-instances <= #(A-oracle circuits of size s) = 2^{poly(s)}; hence a deterministic one-pass machine M_NER with S = log2(#classes + 1) = poly(s) state bits decides L exactly (update by brute force, tau = 2^{poly(s)}). Independent of A. Plug M_NER into the SURVIVED negation lemma: S_M(m) <= s(m)^c for c with poly(s) <= s^c, so the only clause of (40a) that can hold for M_NER is tau_M(m) > s(m)^d. Therefore (40a) <=> [for all M, c, d: if S_M <= s^c eventually then tau_M(m) > s(m)^d infinitely often]. Every corpus result that bounds state count, rank or distinguishability (Q-00adf4fb0a, Q-156fa9c912 syntheses) is capped by log2(#classes) = poly(s) and cannot close (40a).
formula: \forall M\,\forall c,d:\ S_M\le s^c\ \text{ev.}\Rightarrow \tau_M(m)>s(m)^d\ \text{i.o.};\ \text{equivalently } tw(H_{B_C})\le\Psi(m,s,S,\Gamma)<2\,tw(G)+1 \text{ for } S\le s^c,\ \Gamma\le 2^m s^d
dependency_chain: Q-6ead6c935d negation lemma (SURVIVED) + Q-156fa9c912 Myhill-Nerode state bound + PB 9b4160f9 item (3)
break_point: No corpus result bounds tw(H_{B_C}) or any width/state quantity in terms of the update budget Gamma; all corpus lower bounds are space-type and capped at poly(s) by M_NER. Consequence: any valid Psi MUST depend on Gamma, because M_NER (Gamma = 2^m 2^{poly(s)}) exists - a Gamma-free Psi bound is false whenever M_NER is an admissible staged realization (to be checked against the manuscript's admissibility definition).

title: R-MCSP via the generic unfolding bound
statement: Unfolding a De Morgan circuit of size S with r reused gates gives formula size L <= S^{r+1} (each reused gate copied at most S times per level of reuse). With CJW20: S >= N^{(2+beta-eta)/(r+1)}. This is superlinear iff r < 1+beta-eta, i.e. only r <= 1 (by-product: MCSP[N^beta] needs size Omega(N^{1+(beta-eta)/2}) for De Morgan circuits with at most one reused gate). Theorem R needs L <= C S (r+1)^c with polylog dependence on r; the generic dependence is exponential in r. S0029 shows R-MCSP cannot hold for parity-type functions over B2 (r* = 0 but L(parity) = Theta(m^2) > C(m-1)), so the property must be MCSP-specific (Prop R1).
formula: \exists C,c<1,\beta_0\ \forall\beta<\beta_0:\ L(C')\le C\,S\,(r+1)^c \text{ for every circuit } C' \text{ of size } S \text{ with } r \text{ reused gates deciding } \mathrm{MCSP}[N^\beta]
dependency_chain: PB 11bad42d (Theorem R) + CJW20 L(MCSP[N^beta]) >= N^{2+beta-eta} + Q-e7ea75fd10 S0029 (parity r* = 0 over B2)
break_point: generic conversion loses S^r, not (r+1)^c; no MCSP-specific structure result in corpus

title: Space counterexample proved admissible; (8) and (40a) reduce to pure update-cost statements
statement: M_LEX: state = (k, C) with C the lexicographically first A-oracle circuit of size <= s whose truth table extends the prefix read so far (u = tt(C)[1..k], so u need not be stored); on bit b keep C if tt(C)_{k+1} = b, else search the next circuit with tt(C')[1..k+1] = u b; output C or NO. Space O(s log s + m) <= s^2; update 2^{O(s log s)} evaluations; A is evaluated in PSPACE space poly(s). (i) Staged model (manuscript Sec 8 def.): U_t is a fixed Boolean function of S+1 bits, CC(U_t) <= 2^{O(S)}, D likewise; exact on all instances -> ADMISSIBLE, with S <= s^2 and Gamma = 2^m 2^{O(s log s)}. (ii) Uniform oracle-free model of (40a): M_LEX is a plain machine with S_M = poly(s), tau_M = 2^{O(s log s)}. Plugging into the SURVIVED negation lemma: for c >= 2 the space disjunct fails for M_LEX at every m, so (40a) <=> for all M,c,d [S_M <= s^c eventually => tau_M > s^d i.o.], and (8) <=> no admissible C_m with S <= s^c has Gamma <= 2^m s^d. Cell-probe/communication arguments are capped by the state size S = poly(s), so tau_M > s^d for all d requires a superpolynomial computational lower bound for the update map itself.

Attempted: (i) list of all truth tables on k variables: needs 2^{2^k} <= 2^{polylog N} so k = O(log n), complexity <= 2^k/k = poly(n): fails. (ii) Thm 1.7(3): AC0[2^{poly(s)}] refuters exist unconditionally, size 2^{poly(s)} is super-quasipolynomial for s = n^{omega(1)}: fails by size. (iii) CG25: for each fixed b an AC0[qpoly] Student-Teacher protocol for SIZE[n^b]-Avoid exists (Shannon counting; evaluating size-n^b circuits needs AC0 size N^{(log N)^{3b}}), so the size exponent grows with b and no single (absolute) protocol results. Under P = NP an absolute protocol cannot exist (CG25 Thm 1.7), so absoluteness is exactly as hard as the target.

title: Owner formula L = O(S 2^r) verified with the correct reuse measure; consequences derived
statement: Lemma (proved here): for a fan-in-2 De Morgan circuit of size S, let r' = sum over gates of (fanout - 1). Unfolding into a formula, paths(v) <= sum_{parents p} paths(p) <= fanout(v) max_p paths(p) <= 2^{fanout(v)-1} max_p paths(p), so paths(v) <= 2^{r'} and L <= 2 S 2^{r'}. With r = number of gates of fanout > 1 the bound is FALSE (one gate of fanout S/2 over a size-S/2 tree gives L ~ S^2/4); the correct bound in r is L <= 2 S^{r+1}. Combining with CJW20-T1.6: S >= N^{2+beta-eps}/(2 * 2^{r'}), i.e. r' >= (2+beta-eps) log2 N - log2 S - 1. Consequence: MCSP[N^beta] has no circuits of size N^{1+delta} with r' < (1+beta-eps-delta) log2 N - 1. Theorem R premise check: corpus attributes 'MCSP[2^{beta m}] not in SIZE(N^{1+eps}) => NP not in P/poly' to MMW19; the correct source is OPS19-T4, which needs the GAP version; CJW20-T1.6 is stated for exact MCSP, so the chain needs a gap version of T1.6 (not verified). R-MCSP for all circuits would give L <= C S^{1+c}, which for general functions is the open P vs NC1 question; for MCSP no corpus or published structure result bounds r' by polylog.

title: Berkowitz transfer re-checked against superpolynomial monotone bounds
statement: Known superpolynomial/exponential monotone bounds (Razborov clique, Alon-Boppana, Andreev) separate inputs on DIFFERENT levels (k-cliques with C(k,2) edges vs complete (k-1)-partite graphs). On a single slice the Berkowitz pseudo-complement construction makes monotone and general size equal up to O(n log^2 n); so a slice inherits a superpolynomial monotone bound only if it already has a superpolynomial general bound. Transfer of clique bounds to its slices therefore fails; span-program bounds (corpus, <= N+1) are a different measure and transfer to nothing here.

title: Bridge found: the Atserias-Mueller hypothesis implies P != NP (not only P != NP^{parityP})
statement: Derivation (proved here, needs independent check): let sigma(l) >= l be time-constructible with sigma <= 2^{o(l)}. Assume P = NP. By MMW19-T1.2 with A = empty oracle (in PH) and Sigma3SAT answered in poly(sigma) time, search-MCSP[sigma] has a deterministic streaming algorithm with poly(sigma) space and update time; unrolling over the N = 2^l input bits gives P-uniform circuits of size N*poly(sigma) = N^{1+o(1)} deciding MCSP[sigma], hence deciding the promise problem n^{-eps}-MCSP[sigma] for every eps > 0 (YES and NO instances are subsets of those of MCSP[sigma]). This contradicts the hypothesis of AM25 Thm 11. Therefore: [exists eps > 0, sigma as above: n^{-eps}-MCSP[sigma] not in P-uniform-SIZE[n^{1+eps+o(1)}]] => P != NP. A second, independent route removes the parityP oracle inside the AM proof: distinguisher columns have weight <= 8 log(2n) n^eps and their supports {v_p : p in [2n/k]} are enumerable, so the kernel restricted to n^eps <= r^k is in NTIME(r^{k+O(1)}); under P = NP with SAT in time n^c this gives the same conclusion for eps <= delta/(4c) (needs the hypothesis for all small eps). Consequence: the AM hypothesis is at least as strong as (40a) for A = empty oracle (via the same unrolling).

title: Lemma (registered, proved): L(C) <= 2^r (2S+1) for a De Morgan circuit with r reused gates
statement: Let R be the gates of fanout > 1, |R| = r (input variables may be reused freely: formulas repeat leaves). Cut every edge leaving a gate of R; every other gate has fanout <= 1, so the remaining graph is a forest of trees T_out and T_g (g in R), each leaf an input literal or a reference to some h in R; the trees partition the non-R gates, total size <= S. For a in {0,1}^R let T[a] be T with each reference h replaced by the constant a_h. Define F = OR_{a} ( T_out[a] AND AND_{g in R} (T_g[a] <-> a_g) ), where (T <-> 1) = T and (T <-> 0) = NOT T with negations pushed to the leaves (De Morgan, size unchanged). Correctness: let a* be the true values of R on input x. a* satisfies every consistency conjunct. If a satisfies all conjuncts, induction along a topological order of R (T_g refers only to R-gates below g) gives a_g = a*_g, so exactly one disjunct is live and F(x) = T_out[a*](x) = C(x). Size: each disjunct contains every tree once, at most 2S+1 leaves; L(F) <= 2^r (2S+1) = O(S 2^r). Gate-counting convention: S = number of fan-in-2 AND/OR gates, NOT free; L = number of leaves.

title: MCSP[N^alpha] lower bound for circuits with few reused gates
statement: CJW20 T1.6: MCSP[N^alpha] has no probabilistic (hence no deterministic) De Morgan formula of size N^{2+alpha-eps}. A circuit of size S with r reused gates gives a formula of size 2^r(2S+1). Hence 2^r (2S+1) >= N^{2+alpha-eps}, i.e. r >= (2+alpha-eps) log2 N - log2(2S+1). At S = N^{1+delta}: r >= (1+alpha-eps-delta) log2 N - 1. Theorem R would need L <= C S (r+1)^c, i.e. polynomial instead of exponential dependence on r: for r = Theta(log N) the T07 bound gives L <= S N^{O(1)}, which is consistent with CJW for every circuit size; so T07 does not imply R-MCSP. MCSP-specific structural results (S0532 repeated-table restriction, S0479 cofactor bound in Q-10bbdfaf2a) preserve size up to +2 gates under restrictions but say nothing about reuse.

title: Small-threshold regime of T02 against reuse
statement: T02 (MMW19 T1.4(3)) needs: search-MCSP^A[s] has no circuit of size N poly(s) and depth poly(s), s >= m. A lower bound for the decision problem suffices (a search circuit decides). CJW20 T1.5 (s in ((log N)^d, N/(200 log N)]): no probabilistic formula of size N^{2-K/loglog N}/s. With T07: 2^r (2S+1) >= N^{2-K/loglog N}/s, so at S = N s^k: r >= log2 N - (k+1) log2 s - K log2 N/loglog N - O(1) = (1-o(1)) log2 N for s = polylog N. Result: MCSP[s], s = polylog, has no N poly(s)-size circuits with fewer than (1-o(1)) log2 N reused gates - for any depth. T02 needs all circuits of that size and depth poly(s); general circuits of size N poly(s) can have up to N poly(s) reused gates. No published or corpus result bounds reuse of MCSP circuits. CHOPRS scope (exact): their Thm 2 / Prop 39 show (a) magnification hypotheses are satisfied by explicit circuits with small-fan-in oracle gates and (b) the specific known techniques (random restrictions, polynomial approximation, PRG/locality) still work with such oracles. It is a barrier for those techniques only, not an impossibility theorem for R2; T07 itself is NOT localizable in an obvious way (oracle gates of fan-in N^eps cannot be unfolded into formulas of size O(S 2^r)), so the reuse route is not covered by CHOPRS, but it currently stops at log N reused gates.

title: MMW model resolved: search vs decision, target vs computational oracle, update vs total time
statement: T01 (MMW19 T1.3): search version; oracle A appears as gates of the TARGET circuits; the streaming algorithm itself is oracle-free under P = NP (Prop 13 of the manuscript); update time = worst-case time between successive bit reads, final output within O(u). T09 = M_LEX (registered): candidate circuit C consistent with the prefix; on bit b at position t enumerate D with size(D) <= s, D(i) = C(i) for i < t, D(t) = b; keep C if C(t) = b; reject permanently if none. Storage O(s log s + m); A evaluated by PSPACE simulation in poly(s) space (A in PH); update 2^{O(s log s)} poly(s). Correct exact search algorithm. It satisfies the space bound of (40a) and violates the update bound, so it is not a counterexample to (40a); it shows only that the update clause carries the content. Admissible as a staged realization for (8) with Gamma = 2^m 2^{O(s log s)}. QE* admissibility: NOT an O1 algorithm (update not polynomial).

title: Constant-one refuter <=> superpolynomial circuit complexity of a PH language (derived)
statement: (=>) A polylogtime-uniform AC0[qpoly] circuit on input 1^N: each output bit x_i is a depth-d alternation over polylog(N) = poly(n)-bit gate indices with polylog-time uniformity, so i -> x_i is a Sigma_d-time-poly(n) predicate: x is the length-n truth table of a language L_R in PH. A refuter against constant-1 outputs a NO instance: circuit complexity of (L_R)_n > f(2^n) = n^{omega(1)} for infinitely many n. (<=) If L in PH has circuit complexity > f on infinitely many n, its truth table is generable by polylogtime-uniform AC0 of size 2^{poly(n)} = qpoly(N) (as in CJSW Prop 4.4) and is a NO instance there; for the other lengths any output may fail, which the i.o. definition allows. Hence: T03-condition <=> some PH language has circuit complexity n^{omega(1)} infinitely often (more precisely > f(2^n) with f(N) >= 2^{(loglog N)^{omega(1)}}). Known weaker result: Kannan 1982, Sigma2 P not in SIZE[n^k] for each FIXED k (a different language per k). The gap fixed-k -> single superpolynomial language is exactly the CG25 gap fixed-b -> absolute (T06).

title: DISJ: constructive refuter for DETERMINISTIC streaming algorithms (proved), randomized/AC0 open
statement: Fooling set {(x, complement x)}: DISJ = 1 on each; for x != x' one of (x, compl x'), (x', compl x) intersects. A deterministic one-pass algorithm with s state bits after reading x: among any 2^s + 1 prefixes two (x, x') share the state, so A answers equally on (x, compl x') and (x', compl x') (= 1, correct) and on (x', compl x) and (x, compl x) (= 1); one of the two crossed pairs is intersecting, so A errs there. Refuter: run A on 2^s + 1 fixed prefixes, find a collision, output the intersecting crossed pair: time 2^{s+1} n polylog n = quasi-poly for s = (log n)^{f(n)}. Fails T04 twice: (i) T04 requires RANDOMIZED algorithms, whose lower bound is information-theoretic (no fooling-set collision exists for randomized states); (ii) the refuter must be polylogtime-uniform AC0, which cannot simulate A's n polylog n sequential steps. CJSW show no such refuter exists if P = NP.

title: PromiseMAJORITY: deterministic adversary refuter (proved); randomized constructive realization open
statement: Deterministic adaptive A with q < n(1/2 - eps) queries: simulate A answering each query 0 for the first half of the queries and 1 afterwards; complete the unqueried positions once with mostly zeros (p < 1/2 - eps) and once with mostly ones (p > 1/2 + eps); A sees the same answers and outputs the same bit, so it errs on one of the two strings; time poly(n) given A. For RANDOMIZED A with o(1/eps^2) queries the lower bound is distributional (Yao): the refuter must output a fixed x with Pr_rand[A errs] >= 1/3, which requires estimating acceptance probabilities (approximate counting / derandomization); uniform AC0 cannot do this under P = NP (CJSW T1.6). R11's symmetric-circuit theorem is a non-constructive restricted lower bound and yields no inputs.

title: Gap version of CJW20 Thm 1.6 from the proof of Thm 5.5 (owner derivation, assessor-checked)

F is used only (a) on these YES strings (acceptance >= 2/3), (b) on the uniform fillings, where correctness is needed only on the 0.99 NO mass (the remaining 0.01 is bounded by 1), (c) in the PRG step, which needs no correctness. For any K and large N: N^{beta-eps/5+o(1)} <= N^beta/(K m) and N^{beta+eps/5-o(1)} > N^beta, so every probabilistic formula solving G_beta = Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(K m), N^beta] on promise inputs satisfies (a),(b); the contradiction 2/3 <= 0.45 is unchanged. Hence L_prob(G_beta) >= N^{2+beta-eps} for every eps > 0. Consistent with CJW20 remark (gap versions of Thm 1.5).

title: Complete conditional chain R6 -> P != NP; open premise weakened to a size-only hypothesis H_kappa
statement: R-MCSP (C, c<1): L <= C S (r+1)^c, r <= S => L <= 2^c C S^{1+c}. With GAP: S^{1+c} = Omega(N^{2+beta-eps}), so S = Omega(N^{1+delta}), delta = (1-eps-c+beta)/(1+c) >= (1-eps-c)/(1+c) > 0 for eps < 1-c, uniform in small beta. OPS19 (gap MCSP not in SIZE[N^{1+delta}] for all small beta => NP not in P/poly) gives P != NP. The chain uses r only through r <= S, so R-MCSP can be replaced by the weaker H_kappa: every size-S circuit solving G_beta has an equivalent (on promise inputs) formula of size O(S^kappa) for a fixed kappa < 2 (then delta = (2-eps)/kappa - 1 > 0). H_kappa must be MCSP-specific: for general functions it is FALSE (Andreev's function: circuits O(n), formulas n^{3-o(1)}).

title: mSP lower bound for UNSAT_n by monotone projection from CLIQUE (owner derivation, assessor-checked)
statement: Gadgets checked: R(T,a,b),R(T,a,c),R(T,b,c) force T=1,a=b=c=0 (T=0 gives 2(a+b+c)=3); R(p,p',F) with F=0 gives p'=1-p; R(u,v,p') gives u+v=p, so a binary tree with root T selects exactly one leaf; exists z R(a,b,z) <=> not(a and b). Instance: x_{i,v} (k positions, q vertices), one tree per position, R(x_{i,v},x_{j,v},z) for i != j, and R(x_{i,u},x_{j,v},z_{ijuv}) for every pair {u,v}; the last clause is present iff {u,v} is a NON-edge. SAT <=> G has a k-clique. Every clause indicator of UNSAT_n is a constant or a non-edge variable y_uv: a monotone projection (repeated variables allowed), n = O(k^2 q^2) = O(q^4). As a function of y it computes NOCLIQUE(not y) = CLIQUE*(y), the monotone dual. mSP_F(f*) = mSP_F(f) (Karchmer-Wigderson 1993, dual span program) and mSP does not grow under monotone projections, so mSP_F(UNSAT_n) >= mSP_F(CLIQUE_{q,k}). With the cited bound q^{Omega(log q/loglog q)} and log q = Theta(log n): n^{Omega(log n/loglog n)} = N^{Omega(log N/loglog N)}, N = C(n,3).

title: Why the slice step is the whole difficulty (assessor sketch, unvalidated)
statement: Berkowitz-type transfer for span programs: on the k-slice, not x_i = T_k(x without x_i); threshold functions have monotone span programs of size poly(n) over fields with |F| > n (Shamir), span programs compose, and f_slice = T_{k+1} or (T_k and f'). So mSP_{GF(2^l)}(f_slice) <= poly(n) SP_{GF(2^l)}(f_slice) <= poly(n) SP_{GF(2)}(f_slice) (a GF(2) program stays valid over the extension: rank is field-extension invariant). Hence a superpolynomial mSP bound for a SLICE of UNSAT_n would give UNSAT-slice not in parity-L/poly, i.e. NP not in parity-L/poly - a major open separation that still does not give P != NP. The CLIQUE transfer gives a bound for the full function, not for a slice; no known superpolynomial mSP or monotone circuit bound holds for a slice of an NP function, and by this transfer such a bound is as hard as the non-monotone bound.

title: The slice step is equivalent to the general lower bound, not a transfer from the monotone bound
statement: Precise Berkowitz-Valiant form: for the k-slice g = f^{(k)}: mC(g) <= 2 C(g) + O(N log^2 N) (cited by owner, Valiant's improvement; not re-read), and C(g) <= C(f) + O(N log N) (g = (f and E_k) or T_{k+1}). Since also C(g) <= mC(g): mC(g) = n^{omega(1)} <=> C(g) = n^{omega(1)}. For a coNP-hard slice of UNSAT_n (padding with fresh-variable clauses) this is NP not in P/poly itself. Consequences: (i) no 'structure transfer' can carry the exponential monotone bound of UNSAT_n to such a slice without proving NP not in P/poly; (ii) the monotone bound of the full function does not pass to slices in general - Wegener 1985 (cited by owner) gives CLIQUE slices of linear size although CLIQUE is exponentially hard monotonically; (iii) the embedding of a monotone f into a slice (y = not x) is non-monotone and therefore relates mC(slice) to C(f), not to mC(f). Beimel-Nir 2026 (multislice-gate formulas) is a different model (cited, not read).

statement:
statement: LEMMA (variable-length oracle query normalization by a PH wrapper). Let A be any oracle language in PH and let ell>=1. Suppose each of at most q oracle-call slots in a circuit computes an explicit query y of length k<=ell and receives the bit 1_A(y). Put h=ceil(log2(ell+1)) and L=h+ell. Define A_ell on L-bit strings u||v, with |u|=h and |v|=ell, to accept exactly when u encodes k<=ell and v[1..k] belongs to A. Then A_ell is in PH, and replacing each original query with the fixed-length query bin_h(k)|| (y followed by ell-k zeroes) preserves the computation exactly. The transformation adds O(qL) ordinary fan-in-two gates for length encoding, padding, and inactive-slot masking, plus q fixed-L oracle gates. Proof: Parsing the length and extracting the indicated prefix are polynomial-time operations, so A_ell is a polynomial-time preimage of A and belongs to PH. For any original query y of length k, the constructed fixed-length query has prefix bin_h(k) and payload beginning with y; by definition its A_ell answer is 1_A(y), regardless of y's trailing bits. Thus every active call returns the same answer. The query transformation uses O(L) gates per slot; adaptive calls remain valid because each is computed from the same current configuration and prior answers. Inactive slots can use a fixed query and mask its answer. This repairs variable-length padding by changing to the explicitly defined PH oracle A_ell. It does not establish the manuscript's lower-bound hypothesis (8), the MMW update-time premise, or P!=NP.

statement_start: LEMMA (Sigma3SAT^A stage map via length-prefix encoding, no padding invariance). Let M be a deterministic single-tape machine with S work cells over fixed finite alphabet and state set Q. Each update reads one input bit z, then takes at most tau steps and makes at most q oracle queries to Sigma3SAT^A, each query a 3-CNF formula with A-gates of length at most ell. The query string is produced by M as a bitstring prefixed by its length in binary (ceil(log2(ell+1)) bits) followed by the formula encoding. Then the stage map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a single A-oracle circuit with O(tau * (S + log N + log ell)) ordinary fan-in-2 gates and exactly tau*q oracle gates, each of fixed input length L = ceil(log2(ell+1)) + ell, uniform over all x.

1. CONFIGURATION ENCODING (as S0144):
   - Work tape: S cells × O(1) bits
   - Work head: S one-hot bits
   - State: O(1) bits
   - Input head: ceil(log2(N+1)) bits
   Total: O(S + log N) bits.

2. QUERY ENCODING WITH LENGTH PREFIX:
   Each Sigma3SAT^A query is a 3-CNF formula with A-gates. M produces it bit by bit during its computation.
   Instead of padding to fixed length ell, we encode each query as:
   [length_prefix (b bits)][formula_bits (variable, ≤ ell bits)]
   where b = ceil(log2(ell+1)) encodes the actual formula length λ ∈ [0, ell].
   The total encoded length is at most b + ell = L bits.
   This encoding is prefix-free and uniquely decodable.

3. ORACLE GATE INTERFACE:
   Define the oracle gate O_A to accept exactly L-bit strings:
   - If the first b bits encode a value λ ≤ ell, and the next λ bits form a valid Sigma3SAT^A formula, O_A evaluates it.
   - If the first b bits encode λ > ell, or the formula is malformed, or extra bits beyond λ are non-zero: O_A outputs 0 (reject).
   This is a well-defined Boolean function on L bits. No padding invariance is assumed.

4. CIRCUIT FOR ONE MACHINE STEP:

     * Accumulates the formula bits into a shift register of size ell.

     * After the step, the slot holds (length_prefix || formula_bits || 0-padding to L).

Let a deterministic one-pass computation on N-bit inputs have stage circuits U_1,...,U_N, with g_t gates in U_t, and a final decoder D with g_D gates. Suppose each U_t receives the current input bit and the state passed across the preceding input boundary, and outputs the state passed across the next boundary. Then the computation has a circuit of at most Gamma = sum_{t=1}^N g_t + g_D gates computing its final output. If each stage has at most S state outputs, at most S state wires cross each input-time boundary.
PROOF: Connect each stage's state outputs to the next stage's state inputs, and connect the last stage's state outputs to D. Induction on t shows that the connected circuit's state after stage t equals the computation's state after reading the first t input bits, so D produces its final output. Connecting wires adds no gates, hence the gate count is at most the stated sum. The boundary-wire bound is immediate from at most S state outputs per stage.
SCOPE: This is decoder-inclusive accounting conditional on an existing staged realization. It does not construct such a realization for the MMW solver, prove premise (8), or establish P != NP.

title: LEMMA
statement: LEMMA T (decision-to-search transfer; a bookkeeping reduction, NOT progress, closes no obligation). Setup: N=2^m, s=m^c with c>=1 fixed; MCSP[s] is the decision problem on truth tables of length N with threshold s; search-MCSP[s] is as in McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019 Thm 1.4 with empty oracle A (A=empty is in PH). Claim: there is a constant e=e(c) such that if MCSP[s] has no general fan-in-2 circuits of size N*(log N)^(e+1), of any depth, then search-MCSP[s] has no circuits of size N*poly(s) and depth poly(s), and hence NP is not in P/poly by MMW19 Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (s(n)>=n holds since s=m^c>=m). Proof: let C be a search circuit of size S=N*poly(s) and depth D=poly(s). Build a decision circuit: (i) run C on x to get a candidate circuit description of size O(s log s), or bottom; (ii) evaluate the candidate on all N inputs with a universal circuit of size poly(s) per input (valid since m<=s, so input indices fit in poly(s) bits); (iii) compare the N outputs with x and AND them, depth log N. Correctness on every x follows from correctness of the search problem: it outputs a circuit exactly when one of size <=s computes x, and bottom otherwise. The decision circuit has size S + N*poly(s) = N*(log N)^(e) and depth D + poly(s) + log N. Taking k >= e+1 in the decision hypothesis contradicts this, so the decision lower bound with k=e+1 implies the search hypothesis of MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3.

title: LEMMA
statement: LEMMA T' (flag-bit transfer; repairs S0106 and supersedes its step (ii)-(iii)). If search-MCSP^empty[s] is computed by circuits of size S and depth D whose output includes the report bit b, then MCSP[s] (decision) has circuits of size S+O(1) and depth D. Proof: b=1 iff no circuit of size <= s computes T, so NOT b is the decision bit, a single output of the same circuit. Repair of the degree issue: if search size is N*poly(s) = N*(log N)^{O(c d)} for a polynomial of degree d, then with k = c d + 1 the decision circuit has size <= N (log N)^k for large N. Hence H (for every fixed k, infinitely often no MCSP[m^c] circuit of size N(log N)^k) gives: for infinitely many n, search-MCSP^empty[s] has no N*poly(s)-size, poly(s)-depth circuits. Then MMW Thm 1.4 bullet 3 (A empty is in PH, s(n) >= n) gives NP not in P/poly. The constant e(c) is not needed.

title: LEMMA
statement: statement: Tail-negation equivalence for (40a), within its stated class. Fix a time-constructible s with s(m)>=m, A in PH, and the class M_{s,A}^{plain} of uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms with no oracle access during computation, with S_M(m) and tau_M(m) measured in worst case over length-2^m inputs and tau including final reporting. Then the formula (40a), namely for every M in this class, c,d in N, and m0 there exists m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d, is equivalent to: there do not exist M,c,d,m1 such that for every m>=m1 both S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. Proof: For fixed M,c,d,m0, failure of the existential conclusion means that for every m>=m0 neither strict inequality holds. Since the comparisons are complementary, this means both weak upper bounds hold for every m>=m0. Thus failure of the universal formula is exactly existence of M,c,d and a tail threshold m1 on which both bounds hold. Negating gives the stated equivalence. The proof is purely quantifier logic and uses no MMW class inclusion. In particular, the eventual-tail formulation is the exact negation; an infinitely-often violation of at least one bound is sufficient, while a violation at merely one length is not.

title: LEMMA
statement: statement: Repaired oracle-elimination bridge lemma. Let s: N->N be time-constructible with s(m)>=m, and A in PH. Assume P=NP. Then the MMW one-pass algorithm for total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] (MMW Thm 1.2) yields a uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithm M in the class M_{s,A}^{plain} (oracle-free during computation) such that for all sufficiently large m, on every length-2^m input: (i) space S_M(m) <= s(m)^{C1}, (ii) worst-case time tau_M(m) between successive input reads (including final report) <= s(m)^{C2}, for some fixed constants C1,C2 depending only on the MMW construction and the polynomial exponents of the P=NP deciders. Proof: 1. MMW Thm 1.2 (under P=NP, so PH=P) gives a uniform one-pass oracle machine U that solves total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. U uses a Sigma_3SAT^A oracle. Its resources: space s(m)^{O(1)}, update time (between reads) s(m)^{O(1)}, each oracle query length Õ(s(m)), at most s(m)^{O(1)} queries per update interval. 2. Since P=NP, PH=P, so A in P and Sigma_3SAT^A in P. Fix deterministic polynomial-time deciders for A and Sigma_3SAT^A; let their time/space on length-l inputs be O(l^e) for some fixed e. 3. The oracle queries of U have length l <= s(m)^c for some fixed c (since Õ(s(m)) <= s(m)^c for large m). The number of queries per interval is at most s(m)^b for some fixed b. Non-oracle steps per interval at most s(m)^q. Space of U at most s(m)^a. 4. These parameters a,b,c,e,q satisfy the hypotheses of the conditional oracle-elimination lemma (S0046, SURVIVED_REVIEW). 5. Applying S0046: replacing each Sigma_3SAT^A oracle call by its polynomial-time decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass RAM algorithm M with space O(s(m)^{max(a,c,ce)}) and worst-case time per interval O(s(m)^{max(b+ce, q)}). Both are bounded by s(m)^d for some fixed d. 6. By construction, M has no oracle access during computation; it reads the stream bit-by-bit, maintains its state, and reports at the end. Thus M belongs to the class M_{s,A}^{plain} quantified by (40a). 7. Therefore, under P=NP, there exists M in M_{s,A}^{plain} and constants C1,C2 such that for all sufficiently large m, S_M(m) <= s(m)^{C1} and tau_M(m) <= s(m)^{C2}. 8. But (40a) asserts: for every M in M_{s,A}^{plain}, every c,d in N, and every m0, there exists m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d. Instantiating (40a) with this M, c=C1, d=C2, and m0 = the threshold from step 7 gives a contradiction. Hence P!=NP. scope: This lemma closes gap G0001 by establishing that the MMW algorithm under P=NP simulates into the EXACT class quantified by (40a), with explicit resource bounds matching (40a)'s quantification. The proof is conditional on P=NP (for the decider existence) and on the MMW Thm 1.2 resource bounds as stated in the manuscript; it does not assume any class inclusion beyond what S0046 provides.

title: LEMMA
statement: S0001R (repair of S0001, CLAIMED, cross-family review needed). Let A be an oracle with A in PH and let s(n)=2^{n/log* n}. Suppose that for some eps>0 and infinitely many n, every UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on 2^n-bit inputs with poly(s) space has worst-case update time >= 2^{eps n}. Then P != NP. Proof: assume P=NP. Then PH=P, so A is in P and Sigma3SAT^A is in Sigma3^P(A) subset of PH = P, decided by one fixed polynomial-time machine (exponent depends only on A and the collapse). MMW19 Thm 1.2 gives, for an arbitrary oracle A, a one-pass algorithm with space O~(s) and update time O~(s^2) using Sigma3SAT^A calls of length O~(s). Replacing each call by the fixed decider gives a single uniform algorithm with poly(s) space and update time poly(s) = 2^{O(n/log* n)}. Since log* n -> infinity, 2^{O(n/log* n)} < 2^{eps n} for all large n, contradicting the hypothesis on the infinitely many n. Hence P != NP. Scope: restores the contract class A in PH (the earlier A in P restriction was an unneeded easier-oracle restriction); the hypothesis is restricted to uniform algorithms, which only strengthens the conclusion. Premise (uniform update-time lower bound) is G0001 and is OPEN, so this is a conditional reduction, not P vs NP progress. Open points: time-constructibility of s(n)=2^{n/log* n} (log* computable, assumed); CJW20 Thm 1.6 unread at primary source; same-family author (claude-haiku-5-5), needs cross-family review.

title: Decoupling lemma for a shared bit forced to a constant
statement: Finite X; gadgets G_i subset of X x {0,1}; owner projection C_i = {x : exists z with (x,z) in G_i}; shared(T) = {x : exists z with (x,z) in G_i for all i in T}; owner(T) = intersection over i in T of C_i. Hypothesis: for each i there is c_i in {0,1} with (x,z) in G_i implies z = c_i. If all c_i with i in T are equal to c, then shared(T) = owner(T); otherwise shared(T) is empty. Does not cover shared bits not forced to a constant.

title: Private pp-gadgets preserve satisfiability of every index subset
statement: Boolean relations over a finite language Gamma; each R_i has a pp-definition R_i(y) iff exists z phi_i(y, z) with phi_i a conjunction of Gamma-constraints. Instance I = (X, (C_i)) with C_i = (R_i, u_i). Gadget G(I): fresh pairwise disjoint variables Z_1..Z_m, block i is phi_i(u_i, Z_i). Claim: for all S subset of [m], Sat(G(I)_S) iff Sat(I_S). Consequently the minimal unsatisfiable index sets coincide. Exact for private gadgets; no restriction on Gamma, arity or m.

title: Affine codimension-one targets satisfy hypothesis R automatically
statement: Let n >= 1, a in GF(2)^n nonzero, b in GF(2), H = {x : a.x = b}. Let E be a finite set of affine equations over (x, z), with z private auxiliaries, such that pi(sol E) = H and sol E is nonempty. Then for every subset T of E with sol T nonempty, pi(sol T) is H or the whole space GF(2)^n.

title: Gadget-level PP-1g: satisfiability of atom unions
statement: For R(x) = exists y phi(x, y) with phi a conjunction of Gamma-atoms, and gadget copies with pairwise disjoint private y_i. For any set S of atoms, the union of their gadgets is satisfiable iff the conjunction of R(x_i), i in S, is satisfiable. Proof: exists x, exists (y_i) of the conjunction of phi(x_i, y_i) equals exists x of the conjunction of R(x_i), since each y_i occurs in one conjunct only. Constraint-level MUS preservation is not claimed.

title: Single-atom owners: owner-level equals atom-level MUS clutter
statement: Restricted case with no auxiliary variables and every constraint owner a single relation over x (constants substituted): each owner contributes exactly one atom, so minimal unsatisfiable owner sets and minimal unsatisfiable atom sets coincide under the bijection owner to atom. Hence the port property for this restricted case reduces to the atom-level clutter.

title: Common definitional function for shared auxiliaries
statement: Shared-auxiliary GF(2) gadgets E_i(x,z) with H_i = {x : exists z E_i(x,z)}. If there is a function g such that E_i(x,z) iff (x in H_i and z = g(x)) for every owner i, then for every owner set P: {E_i : i in P} is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over i in P is nonempty. Scope: only this common-definitional-function case.

title: Binary-matroid port for GF(2) systems with shared auxiliaries and one equation per owner
statement: GF(2), variables x in GF(2)^n and shared auxiliaries z in GF(2)^k. Each owner i contributes one equation a_i.x + b_i.z = c_i, vh_i = (a_i, b_i, c_i), t = (0,...,0,1). For an owner set P, the subsystem is inconsistent iff t lies in span{vh_i : i in P}. The MUS clutter of owners equals the port at e of the binary vector matroid on {vh_i} plus t.

title: Semantic common-function gadget preserves owner MUS clutter
statement: For constraints C_1..C_m on x in {0,1}^n, any fixed f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k, and G_i(x,z) := C_i(x) AND (z = f(x)) with one shared auxiliary block z: for every owner set S, {G_i : i in S} is satisfiable iff {C_i : i in S} is satisfiable; hence the owner-MUS clutter equals the original MUS clutter. Exact for the semantic gadget only.

title: Graph of f is pp-definable iff f commutes with polymorphisms
statement: For f: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^k and finite Boolean Gamma: graph(f) is pp-definable from Gamma iff f(g(x_1..x_r)) = g(f(x_1)..f(x_r)) for all g in Pol(Gamma) of arity r and all x_i. Proof: invariance of graph(f) under g is exactly this commutation; pp-definable relations are Pol-invariant; Inv(Pol Gamma) equals the pp-closure of Gamma (Geiger; BCKSV). Marked CLAIMED.

title: Affine private gadgets with hyperplane targets satisfy hypothesis R
statement: X = GF(2)^k; constraint i has gadget E_i, a finite system of affine equations over (x, z_i) with z_i private; pi the projection to x; H_i = pi(sol(E_i)) an affine hyperplane of X. For every T subset of E_i with sol(T) nonempty, pi(sol(T)) is H_i or X, so hypothesis R_i holds. Scope: hyperplane targets only.

title: Soundness direction for shared-auxiliary gadgets
statement: Shared auxiliary z. If the original subsystem indexed by S is inconsistent (intersection over i in S of H_i is empty), then the gadget union G_S is inconsistent. Every original MUS therefore contains a gadget-inconsistent set. The converse fails for shared z.

title: Row-space criterion for joint inconsistency with shared auxiliaries
statement: Owners with augmented GF(2) row spaces R_i over (x, z) plus right-hand side. A set T of owners is jointly inconsistent iff e = (0,...,0,1) lies in the sum over i in T of R_i. For one-row owners with row w_i, the MUS clutter over owners is the binary port at e of the matroid on {w_i} plus e, including the shared z-block.

title: Exact MUS correspondence for pinning a satisfiable family
statement: Let H be a finite satisfiable constraint family and u a unit constraint x_j = c not in H. Let H' be obtained by substituting x_j = c into every constraint of H. Then S maps to S union {u} is a bijection from MUS(H') to the MUSs of H union {u} that contain u.

title: Multi-pin MUS lift
statement: Let H be a finite family of constraints on a finite assignment space Omega, and P a finite family of coordinate-value pins. H|P restricts every constraint of H to assignments satisfying all pins in P, with an empty restriction read as contradiction. If S subset of H is an MUS of H|P, then either (i) S is inconsistent before restriction and is an MUS of H, or (ii) S is consistent before restriction and there is an inclusion-minimal P' subset of P such that S union P' is an MUS of H union P. The converse is not asserted.
validation_evidence: The text states it repairs the unit-pin contraction omission and extends the lift direction to simultaneous pins, a stated component of the route, while shared auxiliaries stay open.

title: Multi-pin lift with intersection-of-pins formulation
statement: Let H be a finite family of subsets of a finite set Omega and P a finite family of pin constraints. Write F = intersection of P, with empty intersection equal to Omega, and restrict each h in H to h intersected with F. If S subset of H is a MUS of the restricted family, then either S is a MUS of H, or S is satisfiable before restriction and some inclusion-minimal P' subset of P makes S union P' a MUS of H union P. This proves the lift direction only.
validation_evidence: The text states it proves the lift direction of the pinning component, while shared existential auxiliaries remain unsettled.

title: Projection commutes with conjunction under a single shared witness function
statement: Let X, Z be finite sets and E_1..E_k relations in X x Z. Suppose a single function g: X -> Z satisfies, for every i and every x in X, x in proj_X(E_i) iff (x, g(x)) in E_i. Then proj_X(intersection of E_i) equals the intersection of proj_X(E_i). This does not by itself preserve MUS minimality.
validation_evidence: The text states it is a sufficient condition for projection to commute with conjunction under shared auxiliaries, a stated step of the route.

title: Common-selector projection preserves the indexed MUS clutter
statement: Let E_1..E_k be relations in X x Z and A_i = proj_X(E_i). Suppose there is g: X -> Z such that for every i and x, x in A_i iff (x, g(x)) in E_i. Then for every J subset of {1..k}, the intersection of E_i over J is nonempty iff the intersection of A_i over J is nonempty. Hence J is minimally unsatisfiable for the E-family iff it is for the projected A-family.
validation_evidence: The text states a conditional preservation result under the common-selector hypothesis, which is a stated route step and does not establish that general shared-auxiliary gadgets satisfy it.

title: Equality of projected and lifted intersections gives identical MUS index sets
statement: Let I be a finite index set and A_i subset of X x Z relations. For J subset of I let P_J = intersection over J of proj_X(A_i) and Q_J = proj_X(intersection over J of A_i), with empty intersections equal to X and X x Z. If P_J = Q_J for every J subset of I, then the indexed family (proj_X(A_i)) and the indexed family (A_i) have exactly the same MUS index sets.

title: Common-witness product gadget preserves the indexed MUS clutter
statement: For owner relations R_i subset of X and B_i subset of Z, let A_i = R_i x B_i subset of X x Z. If the common witness set intersection over i of B_i is nonempty, then for every J subset of I, proj_X(intersection over J of A_i) = intersection over J of R_i (empty intersections X and X x Z). Consequently the owner family and the lifted family have exactly the same inconsistent indexed subfamilies and the same indexed MUS clutter.

title: Residual distinguishability lower bound for EXT streaming states
statement: Fix n,s and let L=EXT_{n,s} be the set of prefixes of truth tables of Boolean functions computable by size-at-most-s circuits, with truth-table order fixed. For a prefix p define R_p={z: pz is a prefix of a truth table in Im(Eval)}. Any deterministic streaming machine that decides membership in L after every prefix, whose future behavior depends only on its current state, must assign different states to p and q whenever R_p != R_q. Consequently it has at least |{R_p: p a prefix}| states and at least ceil(log2 |{R_p: p a prefix}|) state bits. Scope: all N=2^n, all s>=0, fixed order, deterministic machines; a state-width requirement only, with no transition-cost lower bound and no simulation of arbitrary H_C. Note: a later record (S0482) reports a gap in the equal-length step of this argument.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0003, a named route obligation, and its statement is a state-width lower bound for the EXT route.

title: Equal-level residual distinguishability for EXT
statement: Fix n,s, N=2^n, a truth-table order and a level t in {0,...,N}. Let L=EXT_{n,s} be the set of prefixes of truth tables of functions computable by circuits of size at most s. For each length-t prefix p let R_{p,t}={z in {0,1}^(N-t): pz is a full truth table of a function computable by a size-at-most-s circuit}. Any deterministic streaming machine that, after reading all N bits, decides whether the full string is such a circuit truth table must reach distinct states after any two length-t prefixes p,q with R_{p,t} != R_{q,t}. Hence it has at least |{R_{p,t}: p in {0,1}^t}| states at level t and at least ceil(log2 of that count) state bits at level t. Scope: each fixed n,s, order and level t; a state-width lower bound only.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0003 and repairs the equal-length step that S0481 lacked, so it states a concrete closure role for a named obligation.

title: Finite residual update as the b-slice of the residual
statement: Let N=2^n and let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For a prefix p of length t<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^(N-t): pz in F}. For t<N and b in {0,1}, R_{pb}={u in {0,1}^(N-t-1): bu in R_p}. Consequently R_p is nonempty iff p has an extension in F, and the residual update after bit b is the b-slice of R_p. This is an exact information-level identity for every finite family F; it gives no bound on the cost of representing or computing the slice for EXT_{n,s} or from an arbitrary MCSP decision circuit H_C.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0004, a named route obligation, while stating no cost bound.

title: Explicit candidate-set transition circuit with address counter
statement: Let F={C_1,...,C_M} be an explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n input bits, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Represent a prefix state by M agreement bits a_j and the n-bit address x of the next truth-table input. For each streamed bit b there is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT transition circuit, correct on valid states, that outputs a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(x)=b] and increments x modulo 2^n. With descriptions hardwired, its size is at most M(s+5)+O(n). Each candidate's equality test costs at most s+5 gates, with one shared NOT b and a ripple incrementer. The record closes G0004.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0004, a named route obligation, with an explicit gate-count bound.

title: Explicit candidate-family transition with M(s+5)+1 filter gates
statement: Let F=(C_1,...,C_M) be a fixed, explicitly listed family of Boolean circuits on n-bit inputs, each with at most s fan-in-two gates. Store one live flag a_j per candidate and the next truth-table address x. On incoming bit b, the update a'_j=a_j AND [C_j(x)=b] is implementable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of size at most M(s+5)+1, plus O(n) gates for incrementing x. For every state and address, a'_j=1 exactly when a_j=1 and C_j(x)=b. It gives no polynomial-in-s,n bound when M is the full circuit-description count. The record closes G0004.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0004, a named route obligation, with an explicit gate-count bound.

title: Explicit-list transition circuit of size M+1
statement: Let C={C_1,...,C_M} be a fixed finite list of Boolean circuits with truth tables E_i in {0,1}^N. At position t<N encode a candidate subset by x in {0,1}^M with x_i=1 iff C_i's truth table agrees with the streamed prefix so far. The exact update on streamed bit b is y_i=x_i AND [E_i[t]=b] for each i. This vector map has a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit of at most M+1 gates, with constants allowed. Under a uniform convention with the column E[t] as fixed data, the bound is M+1 gates. The bound is linear in M and gives no polynomial-in-(n,s) bound when M is the full size-s description set. The record closes G0004.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0004, a named route obligation, with an explicit gate bound.

title: Exhaustive one-pass EXT decision with exponential candidate bits
statement: Fix n>=1 and s>=0. Let C be the set of Boolean functions computed by circuits with at most s fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, constants, and one designated output, on n inputs. There is a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm that decides whether each prefix p extends to the truth table of some function in C, using at most D=1+(n+s+2)(3(n+s+2)^2)^s candidate bits and O(D*s+n+s) elementary operations per streamed bit, with O(D+n+s) working bits. Descriptions with exactly j gates are enumerated for each 0<=j<=s, giving a superset of C; one live bit per description is cleared when its output differs from the streamed bit. This is an exponential exhaustive upper bound for the specified model with no polynomial update bound and no lower bound for arbitrary representations.
validation_evidence: The record states closes: G0004, a named route obligation, with an explicit algorithmic bound; a corrected version (S0534) follows.
